Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 50, verses 6–11:

Explanation of the words:

"Have they not looked at the sky above them?" That is: they are blind, so they do not look with their eyes, reflecting with their minds, at the sky existing above them, so that they would know that their denial of resurrection is not valid.

"How We built it and adorned it." That is: how We built it without pillars, and adorned it with the stars.

"And it has no fissures." That is: it has no cracks that would blemish it.

"And the earth – We spread it out." That is: We spread it out flat.

"And We cast into it firm mountains." That is: mountains, firmly fixed, that do not move or shake, anchoring the earth so that it does not sway with its inhabitants.

"And We made to grow in it every pair of lovely kind." That is: and We made to grow in the earth every kind of beautiful plant species.

"A insight and a reminder for every servant who turns back." That is: We made this an insight and a reminder from Us for every servant who turns back in obedience to Us and returns to Us.

"And We send down from the sky blessed water." That is: rain water, abundant in blessing.

"And by it We made to grow gardens and grain of harvest." That is: by the water of the sky We made to grow orchards, and grain of harvest, that is, what is reaped of wheat and barley.

"And tall palm trees, having ranks of spathes." That is: and by the water We made to grow tall, lofty palm trees.

"For them are clusters piled one upon another." That is: for them are spathes arranged, layered one upon another.

"As provision for the servants." That is: what We made grow of gardens, grain of harvest and palm trees is food for the servants and provision for them, believers and disbelievers alike.

"And by it We give life to a dead land." And We gave life, by that water which We sent down, to a dead land with no plants in it, from the drought and dearth that struck it.

"Thus will be the coming forth." That is: just as We brought forth plants from the dead earth by water, We will bring you forth alive from your graves on the Day of Resurrection, by water We send down from the sky onto the earth, and you will sprout as the herbage sprouts.

Meaning of the verses:

The discourse continues to establish the doctrine of resurrection, the doctrine upon which every reform intended for man is built after the belief in God Almighty as Lord and God. Explanation of the words:

﴿And We know what his soul whispers to him﴾: That is, We know what his self speaks within itself, that is, We know the thoughts and intentions within him.

﴿And We are closer to him than his jugular vein﴾: That is, We, by Our power to take from him and give to him, and by Our knowledge of what is secret and what is apparent, are closer to him than the jugular vein, which is in his throat.

﴿When the two receivers receive﴾: That is, We are closer to him than the jugular vein when the two receivers receive his deeds and record them.

﴿One on the right and one on the left, seated﴾: That is, one of them is seated on his right, and the second is seated on his left.

﴿He does not utter a word﴾: That is, he does not say any word.

﴿Except that with him is a watcher, ready﴾: That is, except that with him is an angel, a watchful guardian, present and prepared to record.

﴿And the stupor of death will come with truth﴾: That is, the overwhelming and intensity of death will come with the truth of the matter of the Hereafter, until the one who denied it sees it with his own eyes.

﴿That is what you were trying to avoid﴾: That is, that death which you used to flee from and dread.

﴿And the Horn will be blown; that is the Day of the Threat﴾: That is, Israfil will blow into the Horn, which is the trumpet, and that is the Day of the Threat of punishment for the disbelievers.

﴿With each soul will be a driver and a witness﴾: That is, with it will be an angel driving it to the gathering place, and an angel witnessing against it.

﴿You were in heedlessness of this﴾: That is, of this punishment descending upon you now.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish the belief in resurrection and recompense. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And the stupor of death will come with truth﴾, that is, however long life may be, death is inevitable, and here it has come: the stupor of death, its overwhelming and intensity, with the truth of the matter of the Hereafter, until the one who denies resurrection and the Hereafter, who denies it, sees it with his own eyes.

﴿That is what you were trying to avoid﴾: it is said to him, this is the death from which you used to flee and dread. His saying, ﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾, that is, Israfil will blow into the Horn, the trumpet which he has held in his mouth since the day the final Prophet, the Prophet of the end of time, Muhammad (ﷺ), was sent, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow the blast of annihilation. ﴿That is the Day of the Threat﴾, that is, the day the Horn is blown is the day of the threat of punishment for the disbelievers. It will be said to the one who came with a driver driving him and a witness witnessing against him: ﴿You were in heedlessness of this﴾, that is, you were in the world heedless of the Hereafter and what is in it; your heedlessness came from your desires, pleasures, and deception by the life of this world. ﴿Of this punishment descending upon you now﴾. ﴿So We have removed from you your covering﴾, that is, We have removed your heedlessness through what you now witness plainly, of the various kinds of punishment, ﴿so your sight today is sharp﴾, that is, keen, by which you perceive and see what you used to disbelieve in and deny in the world.

Lessons from the verses:

1- The demonstration of God's power and knowledge, and that He is closer to man than his jugular vein. Let a person therefore fear God.

2- Establishing the belief that every accountable person has two angels who record his good and bad deeds.

3- Showing that death has pangs, certainly. O God, ease for us the pangs of death.

4- At the hour of dying, every person believes in the Hereafter, for he sees with his own eyes what he used to deny.

5- Establishing the belief in resurrection and recompense by presenting some states and terrors of the Hereafter.

Explanation of the words:

The context continues to establish the resurrection and recompense by mentioning some of its manifestations. His saying: ﴿Who feared the Merciful unseen﴾ is an explanation of the penitent, watchful one, namely one who feared the Merciful, God Most High, while He is unseen by him and he does not see Him, and he did not disobey Him by neglecting an obligation or committing a forbidden act. His saying: ﴿And came with a penitent heart﴾, that is, turning to his Lord, that is, one who turns toward His obedience, by remembering God so that he does not forget Him, and obeys Him so that he does not disobey Him. His saying, God Most High: ﴿Enter it﴾, that is, it will be said to them, that is, to the God-fearing: "Enter it, that is, the Garden, in peace," that is, with greetings of peace upon you, and while you are safe from every fearful thing, such as death, sickness, pain and grief. ﴿That is the Day of Abiding﴾, that is, in the Garden; and in the Fire, for the people of the Garden abide therein and the people of the Fire abide therein. His saying: ﴿For them is whatever they will in it﴾, that is, for the people of the Garden is whatever they desire, whatever their souls crave and their eyes delight in. His saying: ﴿And with Us is more﴾, that is, with Us is for you more of bounty, namely gazing upon His Noble Face.

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The excellence of piety and the honour of the God-fearing before the Lord of the worlds.

2- The excellence of the penitent, watchful one, who, whenever he recalls his sin, seeks forgiveness from his Lord.

3- Explanation of the greatest bliss in the Garden, which is the pleasure of God and gazing upon His Noble Face.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 50, verse 36–45:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And how many generations We destroyed before them⦆: i.e., We destroyed many of the generations before the disbelievers of Quraysh.

﴿They were stronger than them in might⦆: i.e., the generations We destroyed before the disbelievers of Quraysh were stronger in power and more severe in seizing (their enemies) than the disbelievers of Quraysh, and yet We destroyed them.

﴿So they roamed through the lands; was there any escape?⦆: i.e., they searched and explored the lands, hoping to find a refuge from destruction, but they found none.

﴿Indeed in that is a reminder⦆: i.e., indeed in the mentioned destruction of the strong nations there is an admonition.

﴿For whoever has a heart or gives ear⦆: i.e., the admonition is attained by one who has a living heart and gives his hearing, listening attentively.

﴿And he is a witness⦆: i.e., present while listening, with his heart and senses present.

﴿And We did not suffer any fatigue⦆: i.e., no weariness or exhaustion.

﴿So be patient over what they say⦆: i.e., be patient, O Our Messenger, over what the Jews and others say of likening Allah to creation and denying His attributes.

﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun⦆: i.e., pray while praising your Lord before the sun rises, which is the Fajr prayer.

﴿And before its setting⦆: i.e., pray the Dhuhr and 'Asr prayers.

﴿And during the night glorify Him⦆: i.e., pray the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers.

﴿And after the prostrations⦆: i.e., after performing the obligatory prayers, glorify Him with the words of remembrance and glorification.

﴿And listen⦆: i.e., O listener, to what I say to you.

﴿The day the caller calls from a near place⦆: i.e., the day Israfil calls from a place near to the heavens, which is the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis, saying: "O decayed bones, severed joints, torn flesh and scattered hair, indeed Allah commands you to gather for the judgment."

﴿The day they hear the Cry in truth⦆: i.e., the second blast of Israfil, the blast of resurrection, by which they will know the consequence of their denial.

﴿That is the Day of Emergence⦆: i.e., from the graves.

﴿The day the earth will split open from them, swiftly⦆: i.e., they will come out of their graves hastening, after the graves split open for them.

﴿That is a gathering upon Us, easy⦆: i.e., that is a gathering and assembling of people at the place of reckoning, easy and simple for Us.

﴿We know best what they say⦆: i.e., of disbelief and falsehood, so do not despair; We will surely take vengeance upon them.

﴿And you are not over them a compeller⦆: i.e., you cannot force them to faith and piety.

﴿So remind by the Qur'an⦆: i.e., admonish, encouraging and warning, by the Qur'an, and recite it to the believers, for they are the ones who fear the threat of Allah the Exalted and hope for His promise.

Explanation of the verses:

After that grand presentation of the conditions and terrors of the Resurrection to the disbelieving Quraysh, who denied monotheism, prophethood and resurrection and did not believe, thereby exposing themselves to punishment, Allah the Exalted informed His Messenger that their destruction is easy. How many did Allah destroy before them of a generation ﴿stronger than them in might⦆, i.e., in strength and seizing. When punishment came to them, they fled searching for a place to escape to, i.e., to take refuge, but found none. This is the meaning of His words ﴿So they roamed through the lands; was there any escape?⦆. His words ﴿Indeed in that⦆, i.e., in what We mentioned of His words "And how many generations We destroyed before them," are a reminder, i.e., an admonition by which a servant is admonished who has a living heart and gives ear and listens, ﴿and he is a witness⦆, i.e., present with all his faculties and sensations.

His words ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days⦆, the first of which was Sunday and the last Friday, ﴿and no fatigue touched Us⦆, i.e., no exhaustion or weariness. This report is Allah's response to the Jews who said that Allah completed the creation of the heavens and the earth on Friday and rested on Saturday, which is why they observe the Sabbath, i.e., they rest on Saturday. Allah the Exalted responded to them with His words ﴿and no fatigue touched Us⦆, i.e., weariness, since weariness afflicts the worker through the exertion and direct handling of his work, whereas Allah creates by the word of creation; therefore it is meaningless that weariness, exhaustion or fatigue should reach Him. His words ﴿So be patient over what they say and glorify⦆, i.e., be patient, O Our Messenger, over what the Jews and others say of disbelief and falsehood, and seek help in that—that is, in patience, which is difficult—through prayer and glorification before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the night glorify Him, and after the prostrations. This divine guidance and instruction includes the five daily prayers: before sunrise is the Fajr prayer, before sunset are the Dhuhr and 'Asr prayers, and during the night are the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers. Prayer is an excellent aid in patience; therefore when a matter distressed him, the Prophet (ﷺ) would turn to prayer. His words "and after the prostrations" mean: after the five prayers, glorify your Lord while praising Him, such as saying "Subhan Allah," "al-Hamdu lillah," and "Allahu Akbar."

His words ﴿And listen on the day the caller calls from a near place⦆, i.e., listen, O addressee, on the day Israfil calls from a near place, which is the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis, a place near the heavens. The caller, who is Israfil, will say: "O decayed bones, severed joints, torn flesh and scattered hair, indeed Allah commands you to gather for the judgment." His words ﴿The day they hear the Cry in truth⦆, which is the second blast of Israfil, the blast of resurrection, ﴿that is the Day of Emergence⦆ from the graves, and the day on which the deniers will see the consequence of their denial. His words ﴿The day the earth will split open from them swiftly⦆, i.e., they will come out hastening, that mentioned splitting of the earth and their emergence hastening is a gathering upon Us that is easy, i.e., simple with no difficulty in it. His words ﴿We know best what they say⦆ contain consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ) and a threat to the disbelievers of Quraysh. His words ﴿And you are not over them a compeller⦆, i.e., one with power and overwhelming ability by which you could compel them to faith and uprightness; thus your mission is not compulsion, which you are unable to accomplish, but reminding, ﴿so remind by the Qur'an⦆, whoever fears My warning, namely the sincere believers and righteous Muslims.

Guidance of the verses:

1. The legitimacy of warning the disobedient and the deniers of the divine punishment, and that it is near and not distant.
2. For benefiting from admonitions there are conditions: the listener must have a living, aware heart, must give his full hearing, and must be present with his senses.
3. The obligation of patience, and seeking help in achieving it through prayer.
4. The legitimacy of remembrance and supplication after prayer, individually and not in congregation.
5. Affirmation of resurrection and detailing its beginnings.
6. Admonitions benefit people with living hearts.
